source.title: Inherited Goal Drift: Contextual Pressure Can Override Goal Specification in Long-Horizon Agents

assessments.primary_source_quality: Strong primary preprint with open code, repeated-seed experiments, multiple model families, and at least two application environments. No independent replication identified in this pass.
assessments.quantitative_result: The source directly compares target-model behavior from clean starts against behavior after inheriting a trajectory already shaped by goal drift, and reports model-conditional degradation under inherited context. The paper also reports a longer goal-switch conditioning where GPT-5.1 is uniquely consistently resilient among the tested models, and explicitly separates goal identification from behavioral adherence.
assessments.matched_baseline: Good for clean versus inherited drifted history because the target model can be held fixed while contextual history changes. The proposed three-arm O design adds a folded-verified-artifact condition that is not present as a directly tested treatment in the source.
assessments.ablation_or_causal_support: Moderately strong for treating inherited history as an intervention variable and for testing clean reconstruction against contaminated history. Weak for the specific third arm of folded verified artifacts, which is an O adaptation hypothesis.
assessments.reproducibility_or_artifacts: Official code is released; comparator did not independently rerun the study.
assessments.failure_evidence: Direct evidence that a capable target model can inherit a predecessor's failure framing under some tested conditions; stronger-model substitution alone does not guarantee decontamination.
scope_limits: Exact susceptibility is model-family and environment dependent.
Do not infer long context is generally harmful; the causal axis is contaminated inherited trajectory versus clean authoritative start.
The folded-verified-artifact condition is untested and could omit useful recovery context as well as contamination.

original_method_vs_o_adaptation.original_method_evidence: B+ for clean-start versus drifted-history comparison in the tested environments.
original_method_vs_o_adaptation.o_specific_adaptation: C+/B- for the A/B/C O experiment because the clean-vs-full-history axis is directly motivated but the folded-artifact arm and O outcome metrics require O-specific held-out testing.

source.title: Counterfactual Trace Auditing of LLM Agent Skills

assessments.primary_source_quality: Strong current primary preprint with paired with-skill/without-skill trajectories on the same tasks, structured phase alignment, reproducible influence-pattern annotations, and direct software-agent traces. It is still a preprint, covers one main agent family/configuration, and no independent replication was identified.
assessments.quantitative_result: On SWE-Skills-Bench with Claude across 49 software-engineering tasks, aggregate pass rate changes by only about +0.3 percentage points while CTA identifies 522 concrete Skill Influence Pattern instances on the paired traces. The source reports surface anchoring, off-task artifact creation, excess planning, and task recovery effects that outcome-only pass rate misses; moderate-baseline tasks can show more recoverable gain at higher token cost.
assessments.matched_baseline: Strong for descriptive causal auditing: each with-skill trace is paired with a without-skill counterpart on the same task. Remaining stochasticity and the absence of many repeated seeds limit precise causal attribution to the Skill for each individual trace difference.
assessments.ablation_or_causal_support: Moderately strong for the proposition that pass/fail alone can hide substantial Skill-induced behavioral differences and that paired counterfactual traces reveal them. The exact O audit dimensions and retention/selection rule are not validated by the source.
assessments.reproducibility_or_artifacts: The framework is explicitly operationalized on SWE-Skills-Bench and produces structured annotations; this pass did not independently execute the framework.
assessments.failure_evidence: Strong within the 49-task audit that headline outcome saturation can conceal procedure inflation or recovery differences.
scope_limits: 49 tasks and one Claude-based setup are small for general pass-rate effect estimates.
CTA identifies behavioral influence, not automatically whether each influence is good or bad.
Paired traces do not fully eliminate stochastic execution differences without repeated controlled trials.

original_method_vs_o_adaptation.original_method_evidence: B for paired counterfactual trace auditing as a measurement method in the tested software-agent Skill setting.
original_method_vs_o_adaptation.o_specific_adaptation: C+/B- until O demonstrates that matched no-Skill/alternative-Skill trace auditing changes retained decisions or catches regressions beyond existing outcome/cost metrics.

source.title: Imagining Recovery: Inference-Time Counterfactual Realignment for Vision-Language-Action Models

assessments.primary_source_quality: Strong current primary source for robotics/VLA recovery: multiple simulators, multiple VLA backbones and real-world settings, with direct success and restoration-action outcomes. Domain transfer to software/research agents is speculative and no independent replication was identified.
assessments.quantitative_result: CoRe is training-free and, after deviation, imagines continuation from a recent viable state, minimally realigns the physical state to rejoin that continuation, and then returns control to the frozen policy. The primary abstract reports success improvements up to +85.0 percentage points to near-nominal levels and a 42.2% reduction in physical restorations across tested settings.
assessments.matched_baseline: Useful within robotics because recovery performance is compared against disrupted/no-recovery or alternative recovery behavior in the experimental framework. The proposed O checkpoint selector is not directly evaluated.
assessments.ablation_or_causal_support: Strong for the CoRe recovery mechanism in its native physical domain; weak for transfer to O. Preserving completed progress and rejoining a viable continuation is mechanistically analogous, but software/research-agent state has different reversibility, hidden-context and external-effect constraints.
assessments.reproducibility_or_artifacts: Primary source describes simulator/backbone/real-world evaluation; this comparator did not independently run code or inspect full experimental artifacts.
assessments.failure_evidence: Supports the premise that full restart can be unnecessarily destructive/expensive in recovery, but does not establish the same tradeoff for O checkpoints.
scope_limits: Robotics/VLA domain, not software or autonomous research agents.
Physical restoration count is not directly analogous to token/tool/semantic-context restoration cost.
The reported +85 pp is an up-to maximum, not an average transferable effect.
O-specific checkpoint safety must account for irreversible external effects and hidden contaminated premises.

original_method_vs_o_adaptation.original_method_evidence: B+/A- within the reported VLA recovery domain, pending independent replication.
original_method_vs_o_adaptation.o_specific_adaptation: C for a latest-trustworthy-checkpoint selector in O; requires direct comparison against full restart and uninterrupted continuation on matched O tasks with contamination and effect-safety controls.

cross_source_synthesis: The clean-vs-inherited context intervention has directly relevant matched evidence and is stronger than the more speculative checkpoint-folding implementation proposed for O.

Counterfactual Trace Auditing supplies direct software-agent evidence that behavioral and efficiency changes can be large even when pass rate is nearly unchanged, making it a credible measurement operator rather than merely an analogy.
CoRe provides strong native-domain recovery evidence but only weak transfer evidence for O; its exact robotics gains must not be promoted as software/research-agent evidence.
Across all three candidates, the evidence is strongest for experimental axes and measurement methods; the exact O policy choices remain untested adaptations.
